## Energy & Balance Quantities

::: {style="font-size: 0.62em"}
| Symbol | Quantity | Typical unit | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| $E$ | Total energy of a system | kJ | $E = U + E_k + E_p$ |
| $U$ | Internal energy | kJ, kJ/kg, or kJ/mol | depends on context — see note below |
| $E_k$ | Kinetic energy | kJ | macroscopic |
| $E_p$ | Potential energy | kJ | macroscopic |
| $H$ | Enthalpy | kJ, kJ/kg, or kJ/mol | $H = U + PV$; depends on context — see note below |
| $S$ | Entropy | kJ/K | state property |
| $Q$ | Heat | kJ | $+$ = transferred **into** the system |
| $\dot{Q}$ | Rate of heat transfer | kW | $+$ = transferred **into** the system |
| $W$ | Work | kJ | $+$ = done **on** the system |
| $\dot{W}$ | Rate of work (power) | kW | $+$ = done **on** the system |
| $m$ | Mass | kg | |
| $\dot{m}$ | Mass flow rate | kg/s | |
| $n$ | Moles | mol | |
| $\dot{n}$ | Molar flow rate | mol/s | |
:::

::: {.callout-important}
## A note on capitalisation (this offering only)
This course currently uses **capital letters for $U$, $H$, $S$** whether the
quantity is extensive (total, e.g. kJ) or intensive (specific, e.g. kJ/kg or
kJ/mol) — you tell which from context, from an accompanying $m$ or $n$ term,
or from the subscript. For example $H_{sys}$ in the energy balance is
specific enthalpy (multiplied by $m_{sys}$), while $\Delta H_{sys}$ in a
worked solution is often the total change. Future offerings will use
lowercase for intensive and uppercase for extensive properties to remove
this ambiguity.
:::

## Process Variables & State Properties

::: {style="font-size: 0.68em"}
| Symbol | Quantity | Typical unit |
|---|---|---|
| $T$ | Temperature | K or °C |
| $P$ | Pressure | kPa (or bar) |
| $V$ | Volume | m³ |
| $\rho$ | Density | kg/m³ |
| $v$ | Specific volume | m³/kg |
| $x_i$ | Mole fraction of component $i$ | — (dimensionless) |
| $C_P$ | Heat capacity (constant pressure) | kJ/(kg·K) or kJ/(mol·K) |
| $F$ | Degrees of freedom | — |
| $C$ | Number of components | — |
| $\pi$ | Number of phases | — |
:::

::: {.fragment}
Gibbs phase rule: $F = C - \pi + 2$
:::

## Reaction, Mixing & Phase-Change Terms — and Conventions

::: {style="font-size: 0.62em"}
| Symbol | Quantity | Typical unit |
|---|---|---|
| $\Delta H_{vap}$ | Latent heat of vaporisation | kJ/kg or kJ/mol |
| $\Delta H_{rxn}$ | Enthalpy of reaction | kJ/mol |
| $\Delta H_f$ (or $\Delta H_f^\circ$) | Enthalpy of formation (standard) | kJ/mol |
| $\Delta H_{dissolution}$ | Enthalpy of dissolution / mixing | kJ/kg or kJ/mol |
| $\xi$ | Extent of reaction / mixing | mol or kg |
:::

::: {.fragment}
**Subscripts & notation**

- $sys$ — the system · $in$ / $out$ — streams crossing the boundary · $ref$ — reference state
- $i$ — **careful:** used both as an initial-state subscript ($H_{sys,i}$) *and* a component index ($x_i$) — context decides
- $\dot{(\ )}$ — rate, per unit time
- $\Delta$ — change, "final − initial"
:::

::: {.fragment}
::: {.callout-important}
## Sign convention (recap from Ch. 2)
$Q$ and $W$ are always defined as energy transferred **into** the system.
Energy leaving (heat rejected, work done *by* the system) is negative.
:::
:::
